newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising and Media Digest - July 30.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising and Media Digest - July 30.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

CHICAGO - Fast-food giant McDonald's Corp says it has chosen DDB Needham, a unit of Omnicom Group Inc, as its lead advertising agency in the United States, responsible for all adult and promotion advertising activity. DDB Needham, which takes over from Leo Burnett Co, also will be responsible for McDonald's overall brand position and creative direction.
PARIS - French advertising firm Publicis SA says it is signing two separate accords giving the group a 51 percent majority stake and control of the Israeli Ariely and Pelled agencies.

LONDON - Ammirati Puris Lintas Budapest says it has been awarded the advertising launch campaign of RTL Klub, the new Hungarian commercial television channel owned by telecommunications consortium Magyar RTL.

NEW YORK - AT&T says it is in talks with the U.S. Olympics committee and television network to be a long-term sponsor and advertisers. NBC has broadcast rights for the Olympics through 2008. Separately, both Lucent Technologies and UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, say they are in talks to be Olympics sponsors.

DUESSELDORF - The New York headquarters of advertising group Euro RSCG has approved funds for wider investment, paving the way for worldwide expansion, says German unit chief executive Gerhard Schoeps. He also confirms Euro RSCG won the account for a brand-name campaign for Henninger Braeu.
BERLIN - The advertising and beverage industries in Germany step up their campaign to defeat proposed restrictions on advertising for beer, wine and liquor in the face of sinking alcohol consumption.

LONDON - Outdoor advertising company More Group Plc says its Belgium unit acquired stakes in two Belgian outdoor advertising concerns -- Publifer SA and Sape Belgium SA -- for a total of 4.7 million pounds ($7.7 million) in cash.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PALO ALTO, California - Yahoo! Inc says it has formed a global electronic commerce alliance with Visa International and restated its second quarter results to reflect a $21.2 million one-time charge.
LONDON - Leading British booksellers Waterstone's and Dillons each plan to launch Internet sites offering more than one million titles this autumn, the Financial Times reports.

KUALA LUMPUR - After growing 22 percent a month in 1995, use of the Internet is only expanding about five percent a month now in Malaysia, with users voicing concern over the higher cost of local phone calls, according to a new survey.

NEW YORK - ABC Inc says it has named Alfred Resnick as director of digital transmission engineering, effective immediately. Resnick will be responsible for coordinating the transition of the 10 ABC-owned U.S. television stations to digital technology.
LONDON - British publishing group EMAP Plc says it has sold 14 business titles and other assets to Quantum Publishing Ltd for a total of 14.1 million pounds.
MUSCAT, Oman - Oman awards a five million rial ($13 million) contract to Motorola Inc to expand the Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) network in two of its provinces.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW DELHI - Eyeing a big Asian opportunity in compact discs and cassettes, Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc aims to challenge worldwide rivals with its new subsidiary, Sony Music India (Private) Ltd. Sony's strategy is to bring its global repertoire to India and buttress it with homegrown music which it plans to export beyond Indian shores.

PARIS - Gaumont, the French film production and distribution company, say the success of Luc Besson's film, "The Fifth Element", pushed turnover at its film-making division above that of its distribution arm for the first time ever. The film accounted for turnover of 535 million francs ($86.3 million) up to June 30, of which 443 million was made outside France, Gaumont say.

BONN - Daimler-Benz AG is expected to show group net profit more than doubled in the first half of this year to around two billion marks ($1.1 billion) compared with 827 million marks during the first half of 1996, analysts say.

LONDON - LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault may change tactics in his battle to scotch the planned 24 billion pound merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc, The Independent newspaper reports. It says Arnault might put forward plans to sell Guinness' brewing arm and GrandMet's Pillsbury and Burger King food businesses to trade buyers rather than spin them off as separate companies.

BRUSSELS - A senior executive of Swedish brewer Spendrups, the local partner of Pepsi Cola, says the European Commission should not sanction the planned Nordic alliance between Carlsberg and Coca Cola.
PARIS - Pharmaceuticals and beauty products group Sanofi would unload its 49.9 percent stake in Nina Ricci if the perfume house's founders decided to sell, a spokesman for Sanofi says.

CARACAS - U.S. soft drinks giant PepsiCo has slowly regained a toehold in the Venezuelan market it dominated a year ago, although it has still not recovered its national distribution network, a top company official says. Pepsi is now selling about two million cases per month, Ramon Viso, Pepsi's marketing manager in Venezuela says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

WARSAW - United Cinemas International, a joint venture between Paramount and Universal, says it plans to open its first high-tech multiplex cinema in March next year in the Polish city of Poznan. The project is part of the firm's $100 million investment programme to build, under the name of Multikino Ltd, 10 multiplexes in Poland over the next two years.

CHERRY HILL, New Jersey - The annual convention of the National Association to Advance Fat Acceptance draws 400 conventioneers who are fighting for the concept that people should not be discriminated against because of their weight. In addition to seminars and fashion shows, the convention includes a flock of merchants with products geared to the large customer -- oversized furniture and extra-large clothing, among others.
